text: КриптоКиберТерроризм. За чей счет криптообменники сидят в Москва-Сити? Контора в очередной раз нанесла удар по «службе безопасности Сбербанка», правда, теперь это не служба безопасности, а группа «внештатных сотрудников ФСБ» и «Росфинмониторинга». Пока вы отходите от шока, поясним: речь идет об обезвреживании 9 криптообменников в башнях Москва-Сити. Там сидели предприимчивые граждане, которые выводили средства за границу, прямо на украинские счета. Деньги — это плод мошеннических схем. Их украли у российских граждан (начиная от бабушек и заканчивая молодыми мамкиными бизнесменами). Сюр ситуации в том, что мошенники приноровились не просто красть деньги, они еще подряжали доверчивые молодые умы на содействие — инкассация, обработка, обслуживание счетов и прочее. title: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?

The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers". There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form. The BBC has seen details of the investigation into a plot in 2024 in which Russian-linked proxies in Poland and Lithuania not only handled drones and explosives but also delivered them to Germany. The flying bomb The quadcopter was discovered at Leipzig airport late on Tuesday night, forcing one runway into lockdown as a bomb disposal robot rolled into action. text: Удалите сбор на канале! — как часто мы это читаем от бойцов, как сильно мы переживаем и злимся в эти моменты. Мы не понимаем, почему сбор на подразделение является дискредитацией. text: Украинская металлургия начинает останавливаться из-за блокировки портов Компании "Ferrexpo" и "Метинвест" уже приостановили работу. - В августе добыча может упасть на 30%, а ж/д перевозки сократятся на 1,3 млн тонн ежемесячно. - В "Укрметаллургпроме" предупредили что, если морские порты в ближайшее время не возобновят работу, предприятия начнут массово переходить в простой или закрываться. - Закрытие морского коридора будет стоить металлургии $150-200 млн ежемесячно, а производство упадет на 35%. text: 📹 Россияне, попавшие в депортационную тюрьму Швеции, дали интервью Би-би-си Двое россиян, пять лет живущих в Испании, поехали в отпуск в Швецию и оказались в депортационном центре после того, как местные жители позвонили в полицию, рассказали сами супруги Би-би-си. Семен и Татьяна поставили палатку в лесу у озера недалеко от населенного пункта Фурувик на восточном побережье Швеции. Утром 5 августа к ним подошли двое местных мужчин и спросили, что они тут делают, а вскоре приехала полиция. Супругов забрали в полицейский участок в Стокгольме, где сообщили, что они признаются угрозой национальной безопасности Швеции. Никаких обвинений им не предъявили. «Я просто в шоке был, — рассказывает Семен, — Оказалось, что двое местных увидели нас, услышали, что мы говорим с русским акцентом, что у нас есть рации и кейс для ноутбука, и вызвали полицию». По словам супругов, ноутбука у них не было и местные, вероятно, приняли за него черный чехол для удочек, а туристические рации небольшого радиуса действия они взяли с собой, чтобы не заблудиться в лесу без мобильной связи. Сейчас супруги содержатся раздельно, но у обоих в камере есть компьютер с интернетом, поэтому корреспондентка Би-би-си смогла

text: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power Aug. 7, 2026 A partially flooded street in the Smolensk region. Social media A powerful storm pummeled parts of western Russia’s Smolensk region, with strong wind and heavy rain on Thursday evening, leaving thousands without power and downing many trees, including two in the capital city that killed a child and an elderly woman. Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). The regional government initially said 15,000 energy customers were left without power as of late Thursday. By Friday, that number more than doubled to 32,500. While regional Governor Vasily Anokhin established a 24-hour emergency response task force, officials clarified that a formal state of emergency has not been declared. In total, the severe weather disrupted eight central and western districts surrounding Smolensk, an area encompassing more than half of the region’s 857,000 residents. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

text: Ukrainian Attack Sparks Fire at Wildberries Facility in Yekaterinburg Aug. 7, 2026 A fire at a Wildberries logistics center in the city of Yekaterinburg. @exilenova_plus / Telegram A Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a logistics center belonging to online retailer Wildberries in the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, regional officials and the company said Friday morning. Acting Sverdlovsk region Governor Denis Pasler said air defense forces shot down eight drones over the region, three of which crashed onto the roof of the facility. Wildberries confirmed that a fire broke out at the logistics center, located nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the Ukrainian border, but said that firefighters have since contained the blaze. President Vladimir Putin’s envoy to the Urals Federal District, Artyom Zhoga, said 800 people had been evacuated from the facility. No injuries were reported. Wildberries said most of the inventory at the Yekaterinburg logistics center remained undamaged. Inbound shipments were temporarily rerouted to other logistics hubs, the company added. title: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
text: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved? Image source, Jens Schlueter/Getty Images Image caption, A special robot was sent to remove the detonator from the device By Sarah Rainsford Southern and Eastern Europe correspondent Published 7 August 2026, 09:48 BST As Germany investigates how a drone loaded with explosives reached a runway at Leipzig airport, there is renewed talk in Europe of hybrid war. The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers". There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form. The BBC has seen details of the investigation into a plot in 2024 in which Russian-linked proxies in Poland and Lithuania not only handled drones and explosives but also delivered them to Germany. The flying bomb The quadcopter was discovered at Leipzig airport late on Tuesday night, forcing one runway into lockdown as a bomb disposal robot rolled into action. On the tarmac close by were several Ukrainian Antonov cargo planes, stripes along their enormous bodies in the blue and yellow of the country's flag.

Вучич — сбитый летчик, до сих пор раскинувший пятую точку сразу на двух, а то и трех стульях. Правда, ему уже периодически дают под причинное место, требуя быстрее освободить пространство. Перезревший и опротивевший президент только по паспорту сербский. На деле — он встроен в систему евросодома, в глобальную ТНК, он — её винтик, исполнитель определенного градуса. Других там не держут, даже в Сербии. Последний настоящий сербский лидер Милошевич был умерщвлен в Гааге, потому что по духу был русским. А такое в содоме не прощают. text: Кто такие бандеровцы. Осень 1988 г. Западная Украина. Львовская область. Мы — первокурсники ЛВВПУ на полевом выходе под н.п. Старичи. У нас трехдневный марш-бросок во Львов. С непривычки тяжко. А офицеры и "сверчки" (сверхсрочники) нам устраивают квесты. Ночь. Курсанты из числа военнослужащих, поступивших с армии, шалят и "кошмарят" курсантов бывших школьников в окопах и палатках, чтоб "служба мёдом не казалась" — кидают дымшашки, стреляют холостыми. Если кто куда-то не туда в впотьмах положил/прислонил автомат, тут же оприходуют его. В общем, залетели в палатку к спящим вповалку курсачам, заорали что-то, дали очередь. Ступор. Все офигели. Бардак. Паника. Володя Горишняк был курсантом из Мукачево. Проснулся, смекнул, что к чему. Думал секунду и дал: "Хлопци! Я свий! Я с захидной Украины!". Наверное, думал, что пришли свои. Никто его не отчислил за такое, не выгнал из училища. Его даже не разбирали на комсомольском собрании. А ведь хохлов у нас было почти полкурса "мурзилок" (военных журналистов)" и "балалаек" (культпросветработников). Так вот. До распада СССР еще три года. Но всё прогнило уже тогда. И бандеры знали, что кричать и говорить, когда становилось страшно… Порода эта ведо

text: Американская компания BlackSea Technologies (Балтимор), наладившая крупносерийный выпуск безэкипажных катеров GARC ( Global Autonomous Reconnaissance Craft ), масштабирует украинский опыт применения морских дронов на нужды Пентагона. Поставляемые ВМС США (в том числе в дивизион USVRON 3 и для учений RIMPAC) 16-футовые платформы GARC отрабатывают не только роль камикадзе с 450-килограммовой боевой частью, но и функции «маток»-носителей. В рамках спецпроектов (модули Marionette ) компания исследует диверсионные и асимметричные возможности БЭК: транспортировку и запуск FPV-дронов (включая мультикоптеры и БПЛА на оптиковолокне). Это позволяет превратить безэкипажный катер в скрытный плавучий пусковой рубеж, расширяющий радиус поражения FPV-авиации в прибрежной зоне без привлечения пилотируемых судов. Можно, конечно, посмеяться с того, что американцы опаздывают в развитии вооружений, которыми и ВСУ и РФ пользуются уже пару лет (а создали и того раньше), однако нужно заметить, что BlackSea Technologies это частная компания, а не господрядчик вроде Lockheed Martin. Интересно также, что катер предусматривает возможность авиадесантирования, то есть для проведения операции его можно сбросить
author: Boris Rozhin

Они уже и так во всю пользуются сербскими снарядами, минами, САУ. Расчет, видимо, на то, что всего этого в Киев будет передано из Сербии много больше. Вучич — сбитый летчик, до сих пор раскинувший пятую точку сразу на двух, а то и трех стульях. Правда, ему уже периодически дают под причинное место, требуя быстрее освободить пространство. Вучич осточертел многим сербам, его презирают на западе. Но что подвигло его пойти на демонстративный жест, встречаясь и лебезя с врагом России? Всё просто. Перезревший и опротивевший президент только по паспорту сербский. На деле — он встроен в систему евросодома, в глобальную ТНК, он — её винтик, исполнитель определенного градуса. Других там не держат, даже в Сербии. Последний настоящий сербский лидер Милошевич был умерщвлен в Гааге, потому что по духу был русским. А такое в содоме не прощают. А Вучич — не то что не русский, он и не сербский… Как в поговорке: «Ни в мать, ни в отца, а в проезжего молодца». И встреча Вучича с нарколыгой — всего лишь жест, кричащий: « Я свой! title: Key Republican says he will vote for Todd Blanche to become attorney general after other senators defect – live
text: 11.02 EDT Cassidy says he will vote to confirm Todd Blanche as attorney general: 'I will be criticized for this vote' Senator Bill Cassidy , the last Republican who was undecided about Todd Blanche’s nomination as attorney general, said he would vote to confirm Blanche . He noted that while Blanche, who previously served as Donald Trump’s personal lawyer, is “not perfect” , it is ultimately a decision between him or “another acting attorney general who may not run the department effectively”. “This is not a referendum on President Trump. It is a decision regarding Mr Blanche in very specific circumstances,” Cassidy said on the Senate floor, explaining his decision process. His “yes” vote, will now likely clear the way for Blanche to receive the 50 votes needed. Vice-president JD Vance will then cast a tie-breaking vote that will ensure Blanche’s confirmation.

text: Патологический лжец, изменник Родины и претендент на пожизненное заключение взят в плен Харьковской области Рубан Роман Анатольевич (25.01.1992 г.р.), 35-я бригада морской пехоты . Военнопленный играет роль невинной жертвы киевского режима, жертвы обстоятельств и просто недалекого человека, который по глупости выехал из России на Украину, где был мобилизован. Рубан родом из села Большая Кардашинка Херсонской области Российской Федерации. Всю жизнь проработал учителем, однако после воссоединения региона с Россией решил отказаться от профессии и, с высокой долей вероятности, был наводчиком ВСУ . Его родной брат с 2019 года служит в украинской армии, а до этого был в управлении государственной охраны Украины (аналог российской ФСО). В 2024 году Рубан получил гражданство Российской Федерации . Однако паспорт Украины сохранил для реализации своих дальнейших намерений. В 2025 году смог выехать на территорию Белоруссии , где пересёк границу с бывшей УССР и приехал в Николаев. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). While regional Governor Vasily Anokhin established a 24-hour emergency response task force, officials clarified that a formal state of emergency has not been declared. text: Русская армия уничтожила три сухогруза и логистический узел ВСУ в Изюме Минувшей ночью русская армия продолжила наносить удары по морским судам, задействованным в интересах ВСУ. Были уничтожены три сухогруза, которые перевозили военные грузы противника. Кроме этого, были нанесены удары по логистическим узлам украинской армии в Харьковской и Днепропетровской областях. В городе Изюм Харьковской области точным ударом был уничтожен объект транспортно-логистической компании Delivery. Известно, что данная площадка активно применялась противником для доставки и скрытного хранения различных военных грузов, включая беспилотные летательные аппараты и комплектующие к ним. В Днепропетровской области бойцы РФ ударили по железнодорожной станции Эрастовка. В результате атаки серьезные повреждения получили локомотив, а также ключевые объекты местной железнодорожной инфраструктуры. title: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power
text: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power Aug. 7, 2026 A partially flooded street in the Smolensk region. Social media A powerful storm pummeled parts of western Russia’s Smolensk region, with strong wind and heavy rain on Thursday evening, leaving thousands without power and downing many trees, including two in the capital city that killed a child and an elderly woman. Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). The regional government initially said 15,000 energy customers were left without power as of late Thursday. By Friday, that number more than doubled to 32,500. While regional Governor Vasily Anokhin established a 24-hour emergency response task force, officials clarified that a formal state of emergency has not been declared. In total, the severe weather disrupted eight central and western districts surrounding Smolensk, an area encompassing more than half of the region’s 857,000 residents. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

These are people who work for the West and hold Western values,” Zhuravlyov told reporters outside the Supreme Court building. Without providing evidence, Zhuravlyov claimed Rodina had uncovered various violations committed by Yabloko. In response, Yabloko threatened to sue Zhuravlyov, who serves in the State Duma as a member of the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party, for defamation over his remarks. Russia’s Supreme Court confirmed receiving Rodina’s disqualification filing earlier on Friday. A hearing is scheduled for Aug. 10. title: Ukrainian Attack Sparks Fire at Wildberries Facility in Yekaterinburg
text: Ukrainian Attack Sparks Fire at Wildberries Facility in Yekaterinburg Aug. 7, 2026 A fire at a Wildberries logistics center in the city of Yekaterinburg. @exilenova_plus / Telegram A Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a logistics center belonging to online retailer Wildberries in the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, regional officials and the company said Friday morning. Acting Sverdlovsk region Governor Denis Pasler said air defense forces shot down eight drones over the region, three of which crashed onto the roof of the facility. Wildberries confirmed that a fire broke out at the logistics center, located nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the Ukrainian border, but said that firefighters have since contained the blaze. President Vladimir Putin’s envoy to the Urals Federal District, Artyom Zhoga, said 800 people had been evacuated from the facility. No injuries were reported. Wildberries said most of the inventory at the Yekaterinburg logistics center remained undamaged. Inbound shipments were temporarily rerouted to other logistics hubs, the company added. The interior minister is warning of a "new level of danger" from an attack that "may involve foreign powers". There is no proof at this stage to link the flying bomb directly to Russia, which denies any role. But as well as the means and the motive, Moscow does have form. title: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past
text: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past Europe To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. Accept Manage my choices One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Try again Cover image: FOCUS © FRANCE 24 05:34 Issued on: 07/08/2026 - 10:57 05:34 min Share From the show Reading time 1 min In 1894, when the Belgian city of Antwerp was hosting a World's Fair, 144 Congolese people were forcibly brought to the city to be exhibited in the Congo Pavilion. In this "human zoo", seven Congolese men ultimately died of disease. Today, this shocking episode still haunts Belgium as one of its colonial history's darkest chapters. But in May of this year, the city of Antwerp began to confront this painful past by heeding demands from its Congolese community by unveiling a monument to the victims. It's a way to confront the demons of the wealthy Belgian port city that greatly benefitted from the colonial period. FRANCE 24's Alix Le Bourdon reports. text: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power Aug. 7, 2026 A partially flooded street in the Smolensk region. Social media A powerful storm pummeled parts of western Russia’s Smolensk region, with strong wind and heavy rain on Thursday evening, leaving thousands without power and downing many trees, including two in the capital city that killed a child and an elderly woman. Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). The regional government initially said 15,000 energy customers were left without power as of late Thursday. By Friday, that number more than doubled to 32,500. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

title: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past
text: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past Europe To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. Accept Manage my choices One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Try again Cover image: FOCUS © FRANCE 24 05:34 Issued on: 07/08/2026 - 10:57 05:34 min Share From the show Reading time 1 min In 1894, when the Belgian city of Antwerp was hosting a World's Fair, 144 Congolese people were forcibly brought to the city to be exhibited in the Congo Pavilion. In this "human zoo", seven Congolese men ultimately died of disease. Today, this shocking episode still haunts Belgium as one of its colonial history's darkest chapters. But in May of this year, the city of Antwerp began to confront this painful past by heeding demands from its Congolese community by unveiling a monument to the victims. It's a way to confront the demons of the wealthy Belgian port city that greatly benefitted from the colonial period. FRANCE 24's Alix Le Bourdon reports. title: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power
text: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power Aug. 7, 2026 A partially flooded street in the Smolensk region. Social media A powerful storm pummeled parts of western Russia’s Smolensk region, with strong wind and heavy rain on Thursday evening, leaving thousands without power and downing many trees, including two in the capital city that killed a child and an elderly woman. Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). The regional government initially said 15,000 energy customers were left without power as of late Thursday. By Friday, that number more than doubled to 32,500. While regional Governor Vasily Anokhin established a 24-hour emergency response task force, officials clarified that a formal state of emergency has not been declared. In total, the severe weather disrupted eight central and western districts surrounding Smolensk, an area encompassing more than half of the region’s 857,000 residents. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

title: Nationalist Rodina Party Sues to Disqualify Yabloko From State Duma Elections
text: Nationalist Rodina Party Sues to Disqualify Yabloko From State Duma Elections Aug. 7, 2026 Yabloko candidates running in the State Duma elections. yabloko.ru The small nationalist Rodina party has filed a lawsuit with Russia’s Supreme Court seeking to disqualify the liberal Yabloko party from upcoming State Duma elections, Rodina leader Alexei Zhuravlyov announced Friday. “The Yabloko party is full of traitors. These are people who work for the West and hold Western values,” Zhuravlyov told reporters outside the Supreme Court building. Without providing evidence, Zhuravlyov claimed Rodina had uncovered various violations committed by Yabloko. In response, Yabloko threatened to sue Zhuravlyov, who serves in the State Duma as a member of the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party, for defamation over his remarks. Russia’s Supreme Court confirmed receiving Rodina’s disqualification filing earlier on Friday. A hearing is scheduled for Aug. 10. The legal action follows a public clash between Zhuravlyov and Yabloko chairman Nikolay Rybakov during a Central Election Commission meeting last week. news Central Election Commission Bars Yabloko Candidates From St. Petersburg Ballot Read more El

Together with Russia’s Interior Ministry, the FSB targeted nine unauthorized financial channels accused of laundering money stolen from Russian citizens by phone fraudsters. title: Ukrainian Attack Sparks Fire at Wildberries Facility in Yekaterinburg
text: Ukrainian Attack Sparks Fire at Wildberries Facility in Yekaterinburg Aug. 7, 2026 A fire at a Wildberries logistics center in the city of Yekaterinburg. @exilenova_plus / Telegram A Ukrainian drone attack set fire to a logistics center belonging to online retailer Wildberries in the Urals city of Yekaterinburg, regional officials and the company said Friday morning. Acting Sverdlovsk region Governor Denis Pasler said air defense forces shot down eight drones over the region, three of which crashed onto the roof of the facility. Wildberries confirmed that a fire broke out at the logistics center, located nearly 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) from the Ukrainian border, but said that firefighters have since contained the blaze. President Vladimir Putin’s envoy to the Urals Federal District, Artyom Zhoga, said 800 people had been evacuated from the facility. No injuries were reported. Wildberries said most of the inventory at the Yekaterinburg logistics center remained undamaged. Inbound shipments were temporarily rerouted to other logistics hubs, the company added. Videos shared on social media showed employees evacuating the facility as drones struck the roof, with gunfire audible i

title: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past
text: Antwerp's 'human zoo': Belgium confronts shame of colonial past Europe To display this content from YouTube, you must enable advertisement tracking and audience measurement. Accept Manage my choices One of your browser extensions seems to be blocking the video player from loading. To watch this content, you may need to disable it on this site. Try again Cover image: FOCUS © FRANCE 24 05:34 Issued on: 07/08/2026 - 10:57 05:34 min Share From the show Reading time 1 min In 1894, when the Belgian city of Antwerp was hosting a World's Fair, 144 Congolese people were forcibly brought to the city to be exhibited in the Congo Pavilion. In this "human zoo", seven Congolese men ultimately died of disease. Today, this shocking episode still haunts Belgium as one of its colonial history's darkest chapters. But in May of this year, the city of Antwerp began to confront this painful past by heeding demands from its Congolese community by unveiling a monument to the victims. It's a way to confront the demons of the wealthy Belgian port city that greatly benefitted from the colonial period. FRANCE 24's Alix Le Bourdon reports. title: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
text: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved? title: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power
text: Deadly Storm Batters Smolensk Region, Leaving Thousands Without Power Aug. 7, 2026 A partially flooded street in the Smolensk region. Social media A powerful storm pummeled parts of western Russia’s Smolensk region, with strong wind and heavy rain on Thursday evening, leaving thousands without power and downing many trees, including two in the capital city that killed a child and an elderly woman. Emergency services said the two deaths took place in separate parts of the regional capital of Smolensk, which bore the brunt of the storm as winds reached gusts of up to 20 meters per second (45 miles per hour). The regional government initially said 15,000 energy customers were left without power as of late Thursday. By Friday, that number more than doubled to 32,500. While regional Governor Vasily Anokhin established a 24-hour emergency response task force, officials clarified that a formal state of emergency has not been declared. In total, the severe weather disrupted eight central and western districts surrounding Smolensk, an area encompassing more than half of the region’s 857,000 residents. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

title: Nationalist Rodina Party Sues to Disqualify Yabloko From State Duma Elections
text: Nationalist Rodina Party Sues to Disqualify Yabloko From State Duma Elections Aug. 7, 2026 Yabloko candidates running in the State Duma elections. yabloko.ru The small nationalist Rodina party has filed a lawsuit with Russia’s Supreme Court seeking to disqualify the liberal Yabloko party from upcoming State Duma elections, Rodina leader Alexei Zhuravlyov announced Friday. “The Yabloko party is full of traitors. These are people who work for the West and hold Western values,” Zhuravlyov told reporters outside the Supreme Court building. Without providing evidence, Zhuravlyov claimed Rodina had uncovered various violations committed by Yabloko. In response, Yabloko threatened to sue Zhuravlyov, who serves in the State Duma as a member of the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party, for defamation over his remarks. Russia’s Supreme Court confirmed receiving Rodina’s disqualification filing earlier on Friday. A hearing is scheduled for Aug. 10. title: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial
text: Former Popcorn Books Publisher Receives Suspended Sentence in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Trial Aug. 7, 2026 Dmitry Protopopov. Sergei Vedyashkin / Moskva News Agency A Moscow judge handed down a four-year suspended sentence on Friday to the former head of the independent publishing houses Popcorn Books and Individuum after finding him guilty of LGBTQ+ “extremism.” Dmitry Protopopov was among three senior managers arrested in May 2025 and charged with “extremism” following a 2023 ruling by Russia’s Supreme Court to outlaw the so-called “ international LGBT movement, ” thereby making it a criminal offense to publish, sell or distribute literature with LGBTQ+ themes. Prosecutors accused Protopopov and his colleagues of devising a scheme that would allow them to sell books with LGBTQ+ themes to “loyal customers” in an effort to avoid writing off 10 million rubles ($121,700) in losses. In addition to the suspended sentence, a judge from the Zamoskvoretsky District Court placed Protopopov on probation for five years and banned him from working in publishing or managing websites for four years, granting the prosecution’s request in full. news CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGB

These are people who work for the West and hold Western values,” Zhuravlyov told reporters outside the Supreme Court building. In response, Yabloko threatened to sue Zhuravlyov, who serves in the State Duma as a member of the nationalist Liberal Democratic Party, for defamation over his remarks. Russia’s Supreme Court confirmed receiving Rodina’s disqualification filing earlier on Friday. A hearing is scheduled for Aug. 10. text: German airport drone-bomb: Could Russia be involved?
